extracted.intended_audience: journalism scholars, media studies researchers, journalism students, and news editors interested in selection/gatekeeping
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying criteria that an editor (gatekeeper) uses to accept or reject news items (wire copy), based on White's empirical case study of Mr. Gates. Useful for analyzing newsworthiness decisions and editorial selection behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Not interesting"
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal taste judgment that the story would not engage readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by the editor as a subjective assessment of reader interest; no further specification — effectively 'not newsworthy' because it won't engage the paper's audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Dull writing"
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire copy stylistically unappealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection based on writing quality or style rather than substance; indicates emphasis on readable, engaging prose for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: "No good"
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic dismissal reflecting unspecified editorial intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all subjective rejection indicating the editor's overall negative sense of the item without a stated reason; signals reliance on tacit editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: "B.S."
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories Mr. Gates judged exaggerated, propagandistic, or untrustworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection for perceived lack of credibility or for material seen as spin/misinformation; reflects gatekeeper's trust standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Propaganda"
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories pushing a political or institutional agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items perceived as advocacy rather than neutral reporting were excluded; editor filters out content seen as agenda-driven.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Don't care for suicides"
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal moral aversion (extends to other taboo topics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection on the basis of the editor's moral/ethical preferences about subject matter; indicates topic-level taboos can determine selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Too far away"
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic remoteness from the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor excludes items deemed geographically irrelevant to the paper's local/regional audience; proximity is a dimension of newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Too Red"
rubrics_metrics.description: Political ideology Mr. Gates personally opposed (anti-Communist filter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideological bias in selection: content reflecting disfavored political positions may be rejected; demonstrates political disposition shaping coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Sour grapes"
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories about complaints, recriminations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items focused on grievances or petty disputes were dismissed as unworthy; editor filters out certain topical genres (e.g., complaint-driven pieces).

rubrics_metrics.name: "Never use this"
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorical exclusion of topic types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute exclusion rule applied by the gatekeeper to some categories of stories; indicates hard boundaries in editorial selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: "No space"
rubrics_metrics.description: Page-fit constraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanical rejection based on physical layout and column/inch limitations; a pragmatic constraint distinct from content judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Would use if space"
rubrics_metrics.description: Marginal stories rejected for layout reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates stories that are acceptable in content but turned down only because of current space scarcity; suggests conditional acceptance contingent on resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Used another story"
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplicate / overlapping coverage of same event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection among substitutes: when multiple items cover the same event, some are rejected because another story is chosen to represent it.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Too late — no space"
rubrics_metrics.description: Filed after deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal constraint causing rejection; timeliness and production deadlines affect whether material can be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Goes into morgue"
rubrics_metrics.description: Useful for files but not for today's edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories saved for archival use rather than immediate publication; indicates a distinction between evergreen value and immediate newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: High rejection/selectivity rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 90% of incoming wire copy was killed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates extreme selectivity in editorial processes; most submitted/received material will be rejected, so selection criteria act as strong filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjective dominance in selection
rubrics_metrics.description: A majority of rejections rested on personal value judgments rather than mechanical constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial choice is driven primarily by individual tastes, beliefs, and assessments; mechanical constraints (space, duplication, deadlines) are secondary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two master classes of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) 'Not worthy of being reported' (subjective) and (b) 'another story on the same event' (selection among substitutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection operates either by discarding items as unworthy or by choosing among multiple items about the same event; these are functionally distinct decision processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gatekeeper reproduces audience model
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Gates's category counts closely matched reader preference surveys he had completed earlier — the gatekeeper reproduced an audience model in his head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors internalize perceived audience tastes and use that mental model to guide selection; claims of objectivity may mask audience-based filtering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal beliefs shape output
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal beliefs (e.g., anti-Communist, anti-suicide aversions) visibly shaped which stories were accepted or rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual ideological and moral dispositions leak into editorial decisions, producing systematic biases in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness as constructed, not intrinsic
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness is not a property of events but the product of an individual decider's experiences, attitudes, expectations, and organizational constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of what is 'news' must account for the gatekeeper's subjective framework and the newsroom's routines and limits; use this constructivist lens when analyzing selection.
